items.title: Zimbabwe tycoon Wicknell Chivayo and wife killed in helicopter crash
items.summary: Wicknell Chivayo was a prominent businessman known for his extravagant lifestyle Prominent Zimbabwean businessman Wicknell Chivayo and his wife have been killed in a helicopter crash that left six people dead, his family have confirmed The helicopter came down in the Marondera rural area, about 70km (43 miles) east of the capital, Harare, on Wednesday evening. Police said all six people on board died Family spokesperson Herbert Chivayo confirmed the deaths of the 43-year-old businessman and his wife Lucy Muteke to state broadcaster ZBC, saying the family was devastated by the tragedy Chivayo was known for his lavish lifestyle, close ties to some African presidents and lucrative government contracts that had repeatedly attracted scrutiny He had denied allegations of wrongdoing linked to his business dealings Police spokesperson Commissioner Paul Nyathi said the aircraft crashed at about 17:00 local time (15:00 GMT) and had six occupants, but authorities did not immediately identify all those on board.

items.title: Volume of currency trading reached 5.73 billion dollars
items.summary: Maputo, 01 Oct (AIM) – Mozambique’s foreign exchange market has recorded a high volume of currency trading between January and August of this year, with commercial banks purchasing 5.73 billion US dollars. On the other hand, the commercial banks sold 5.65 billion dollars to their clients, according to data released on Wednesday by the Monetary Policy Committee of the Bank of Mozambique (CPMO). Speaking to reporters, Felisberto Navalha, governor of Bank of Mozambique, explained that the dynamism of the foreign exchange market has been driven primarily by the execution of liquefied natural gas projects in the Rovuma Basin and the performance of the extractive industry, against a backdrop of relative exchange rate stability. “The behavior of the foreign exchange market reflects economic activity linked to major projects and the extractive industry, sectors that continue to generate considerable demand for foreign currency transactions.

items.title: Mozambique | Fish found dead in the Loreco River in Marrupa
items.summary: Fish were found dead in the waters and along the banks of the Loreco River near Marrangira, in the Marrupa district of Niassa province. The event raises concerns regarding water quality in a region where artisanal mining activity is also present. The cause of the fish mortality has not yet been determined Images released by Moçambique Bio show dead fish concentrated near the water and along the banks of the river course. The occurrence raises concern over a potential change in water quality, but laboratory analyses are not yet available to determine the cause of the animals’ death. The Lureco River is identified in documentation regarding the Marrupa district as a tributary of the Lugenda River, which forms part of the region’s hydrographic network The Lureco area is also known for mining activity. Official 2022 production data records, for example, gold production at the Lureco Camp in Marrupa.

items.title: Bank of Mozambique holds interest rate at 9.25 percent
items.summary: Maputo, 01 Oct (AIM) – The Monetary Policy Committee of the Bank of Mozambique (CPMO), meeting in Maputo on Wednesday, has decided to continue keeping its benchmark interest rate, known as the MIMO rate, at 9.25 per cent. At the same meeting, the CPMO decided to modify the reserve requirement regime, a measure that will take effect starting from the next reserve maintenance period. According to the Governor of the Bank of Mozambique, Felisberto Navalha, the decision stems from prevailing risks and uncertainties associated, among other factors, with climate shocks and prolonged geopolitical conflicts in the Middle East and Europe, which could impact international fuel and food prices. “The decision also comes against a backdrop of slow economic recovery. The applicable interest rate will be the MIMO rate, potentially increased by a 150-basis-point margin, depending on the purpose”, Navalha explained.

items.title: Russian dissident Garry Kasparov says US warned him of danger to his life
items.summary: Garry Kasparov retired from competitive chess in 2005 to found political opposition movements in Russia An exiled Russian opposition figure living in the US says he was warned by American and Lithuanian security services that his life was in danger Former chess world champion Garry Kasparov said he was one of two dissidents told to take precautions, which he had done His comments come after the US Justice Department unsealed an indictment earlier this month charging five people who allegedly work for a network linked to the Kremlin with plotting attacks and murders in countries including the US, focusing on Russian dissidents and defectors Kasparov wrote in his publication The Next Move that he had not been told explicitly that he and fellow Free Russia Forum co-founder Ivan Tyutrin were considered targets, but said both had been warned about their safety Spanish newspaper El Mundo reported that it had obtained information that Kasparov, along with another Russian opposition figure, Ilya Ponomarev, had been warned about the plot over the summer by US authorities Citing sources close…

items.title: Africa's richest man launches Kenya oil refinery despite land protests
items.summary: Aliko Dangote made his fortune in cement before branching into oil Nigerian billionaire Aliko Dangote and Kenya's President William Ruto have broken ground on a $16bn (£12bn) oil refinery in Lamu, on Kenya's northern coast Upon completion, the refinery is expected to process 700,000 barrels of crude oil a day, making it East Africa's largest industrial project by capacity Ahead of the launch, some local residents took to the streets to demand more compensation for land used for the refinery Speaking to the BBC, Dangote, Africa's richest man, dismissed the protests as games played by local marketers and international players, insisting the refinery would go ahead and would be ready by 2030 as planned The ground-breaking was also attended by the leaders of Uganda, Ethiopia, Togo and Benin Dangote has offered regional governments a combined 30% stake in the refinery, according to Reuters news agency "This is Africa coming together to build Africa.

items.title: Five EU states plan first deportation center in Africa for 2027
items.summary: Greece, Germany, Austria, Denmark and the Netherlands are moving forward with plans to establish deportation centers outside the EU. An African partner country has reportedly already been selected Deportation centers are legally contentious, expensive and the subject of political controversy: For years, Brussels has been grappling with the issue of establishing such centers outside the EU for rejected asylum seekers. Previous attempts have failed due to legal objections, but now, a "group of five" consisting of Greece , Germany , Austria , Denmark and the Netherlands believes it has overcome these hurdles During an interview with the Greek television channel ANT1, Greece's Minister of Migration, Thanos Plevris, stated that the first of these so-called " return hubs " is scheduled to begin operations as early as the second half of 2027 — just in time for Greece to assume the EU Council Presidency Plevris said Greece had chosen an African country but could not reveal its name yet.
